criticalBugFoundAndFixed.bug: CMS data-api v1 state filter silently failed open — loaded all 50+ US states' cost-report data instead of just KY+FL
criticalBugFoundAndFixed.discovery: The accuracy check's row-count floor passed with actual=7926 rows where ~1416 was expected. Investigating the DB directly showed rows tagged with every US state code (AK, AL, AR, ... WI), not just KY/FL, each represented roughly twice (once from the nominally-KY-filtered fetch, once from the nominally-FL-filtered fetch).
criticalBugFoundAndFixed.rootCause: The filter query used operator value "==" (double equals). This CMS data-api endpoint requires a single "=" for equality; an unrecognized operator value causes the filter to be silently dropped rather than erroring, so the endpoint returns unfiltered national data. Confirmed by direct curl/fetch testing: operator="==" returned random unfiltered states; operator="=" correctly returned only the requested state.
criticalBugFoundAndFixed.fix: Changed the filter operator to "=" in both RetrieveAndLoadFacilityFinancialDistress.ts and CheckFacilityDistressNumbers.ts. Added a defense-in-depth check that throws immediately if any row in a state-filtered response carries a different state code than requested, so this exact failure mode cannot recur silently in a future run even if CMS changes API behavior again.
criticalBugFoundAndFixed.impactAssessment: The polluted national data never reached any export or UI surface — ExportFacilityDistressForUi.ts filters `facilities.rows.filter(f => f.state_code === state)` using each row's own CMS-reported state_code field (accurate regardless of the broken request filter), so no cross-state leakage occurred in any user-facing output. The bug was confined to unnecessary data volume in the DSO table (7926 rows landed instead of ~1336) and would have made the row-count-floor reconciliation check meaningless (technically passing for the wrong reason). Purged and reloaded correctly after the fix; verified with a direct DB query showing only KY/FL rows post-fix.
